definitions.explanation: A substance with a pH above 7, the opposite of an acid. Used in chemistry, in product descriptions (alkaline batteries, alkaline water), and in nutrition discussions of alkaline-forming foods.

examples.japanese: せっけんはアルカリ{性|せい}だ。
{酸|さん}とアルカリを{混|ま}ぜると{中和|ちゅうわ}する。
examples.english: Acid and alkali neutralize each other when mixed.

examples.japanese: {強|つよ}いアルカリ{性|せい}の{洗剤|せんざい}は{皮膚|ひふ}を{傷|きず}つけることがあるので{注意|ちゅうい}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: Strongly alkaline detergents can damage the skin, so care is needed.

notes:
Loanword from Dutch/Latin via European chemistry vocabulary. Written in katakana.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- アルカリ{性|せい}: alkaline; alkalinity
- アルカリ{電池|でんち}: alkaline battery
- アルカリ{水|すい} / アルカリイオン{水|すい}: alkaline water
- {強|つよ}いアルカリ: a strong alkali

SIMILAR / RELATED:
- {酸|さん}: acid — direct chemical opposite
- {中性|ちゅうせい}: neutral (pH-wise)
- {塩基|えんき}: base — more technical chemistry term, includes alkalis and other proton acceptors
